question: In △ABC, BD ⟂ AC at D and ∠DBC = 71°. E is a point on BC such that ∠CAE = 17°. What is the measure of ∠AEB?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In the right-angled △BDC, the sum of acute angles is 90°, so ∠C = 90° − 71° = 19°.

In △AEC, the exterior angle at E is ∠AEB.

By the Exterior Angle Theorem, exterior ∠AEB = ∠CAE + ∠C.

⇒ ∠AEB = 17° + 19° = 36°.

**∴ The correct answer is 36°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

BD ⊥ AC at D ⇒ ∠BDC = 90°

∠DBC = 71°

∠CAE = 17°

**Calculations:**

In △BDC, the sum of all interior angles is 180°:

⇒ ∠BDC + ∠DBC + ∠BCD = 180°

⇒ 90° + 71° + ∠BCD = 180°

⇒ 161° + ∠BCD = 180°

⇒ ∠BCD = 180° − 161° = 19°

Since D lies on line segment AC, the angle ∠BCD is the same as ∠BCA (or ∠ACE).

⇒ ∠ACE = 19°

Now, consider △AEC. The side CE is extended to B (since E is a point on BC).

According to the Exterior Angle Theorem, the exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles.

⇒ Exterior ∠AEB = ∠CAE + ∠ACE

⇒ ∠AEB = 17° + 19° = 36°

**∴ The correct answer is 36°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exterior Angle Theorem

The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the measures of its two remote (opposite) interior angles.

Sum of Angles of a Triangle

The sum of all three interior angles in any Euclidean triangle is always exactly 180°.

Right-Angled Triangle Properties

A triangle where one of the interior angles is exactly 90°. In such triangles, the other two acute angles are strictly complementary (they sum to 90°).
